Fails the which-came-first test (Law 7). The concept of formants — vocal-tract resonances that shape vowel quality — was established in acoustics and phonetics (Helmholtz's resonator theory of vowel quality, 1863; spectrographic phonetics of the 1930s-40s) long before 'speech processing' existed as a discipline. The concept was fed by acoustics, not by the discipline; speech processing later adopted formant analysis as one of its tools. The pinned direction (speech-processing first, feeding formant) inverts the actual lineage.

Pinned sense names the wrong antecedent (Law 11d). The note says the cepstrum was 'specifically to detect periodic structures in spectra such as formant spacing' — but formants are NOT periodically spaced: formant's own accepted definition makes them irregular vocal-tract resonances determined by cavity shape. The quasi-periodic structures the cepstrum was invented to reveal (Bogert, Healy and Tukey, 1968) are the pitch harmonic series and echoes — the source structure of the log-spectrum. The filer has conflated formants with harmonics. The true lineage runs from pitch/source analysis of speech spectra, not from formant; the pinned DERIVED_FROM antecedent is the wrong node.
